s01_bottom_line.text: Democratic midterm gains increase the likelihood of tougher scrutiny on electricity affordability and grid-cost allocation, creating near-term uncertainty for utilities that trade in line with AI developments, especially those exposed to Texas and Georgia.
The publisher notes policy changes could target who bears grid-connection costs, tax exemptions and financial commitments, affecting utilities tied to the build-out.
The article flags regulatory repricing risk for AI-linked utilities but does not quantify any earnings or revenue impact.

items.text: In the 2026 US midterm elections the Democratic party won control of both the House and the Senate, setting up gridlock with a Republican president.
